findings.evidence: `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:2070` `Handle.UpdateAll()` creates `priv := newMySQLPrivilege()` then calls `priv.LoadAll(h.sctx)` and `h.priv.Store(priv)` but does not set `priv.globalVars` and does not sort per-user record slices after load. `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:435` `MySQLPrivilege.LoadAll()` calls `LoadGlobalPrivTable/LoadTablesPrivTable/LoadColumnsPrivTable`. Those load methods (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:816`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:864`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:873`) only append decoded rows and do not sort. Lookups are first-match: `matchGlobalPriv`/`matchTables`/`matchColumns` return the first matching record in `item.data` (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1378`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1421`, `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:1435`). Sorting is explicitly relied upon elsewhere: merge sorts `itm.data` for these tables (`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:612`..`pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:666`). `pkg/domain/domain.go:2944` shows `NotifyUpdatePrivilege` calls `do.PrivilegeHandle().UpdateAll()` when `event.All` (e.g. `FLUSH PRIVILEGES`), and `pkg/privilege/privileges/cache.go:2089` shows `UpdateAllActive()` can fall back to `UpdateAll()` when active users > 1024.
findings.fix: In `Handle.UpdateAll()`, set `priv.globalVars = h.globalVars` before `priv.LoadAll(...)`. Ensure `LoadAll()` results are ordered for first-match lookups by sorting per-user slices after load (e.g. in each `Load*Table` add `p.<tree>.Ascend(func(itm ...) { slices.SortFunc(itm.data, compareX); return true })` for `globalPriv`, `tablesPriv`, `columnsPriv` (and `db` too), or add a dedicated `p.sortAll()` called at end of `LoadAll()`).
findings.impact: After `Handle.UpdateAll()` (reachable via `NotifyUpdateAllUsersPrivilege`/`FLUSH PRIVILEGES`, and also via `UpdateAllActive()` fallback when `activeUsers` > 1024), privilege/auth decisions can become dependent on storage scan order: `matchTables`/`matchColumns`/`matchGlobalPriv` return the first match, so a less-specific host pattern (e.g. `'%') may be chosen before a more-specific one (e.g. `'localhost'`), potentially granting/denying table/column privileges incorrectly and potentially bypassing or misapplying SSL/login restrictions stored in `mysql.global_priv`. Additionally, missing `globalVars` wiring in `UpdateAll()` can mis-assign `AuthPlugin` when `mysql.user.plugin` is empty (default auth plugin should come from `@@global.default_authentication_plugin`).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `pingcap/master` (at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `Handle.UpdateAll()` still loads via `LoadAll()` and stores directly; `LoadTablesPrivTable`/`LoadColumnsPrivTable`/`LoadGlobalPrivTable` still do not sort per-user slices, and `matchTables` remains first-match, so this ordering hazard is not fully removed upstream.
findings.verify: Add a regression covering the `UpdateAll()` path (not just merge path): create both `user@'%'` and `user@'localhost'` entries with conflicting `mysql.tables_priv`/`mysql.columns_priv` (and `mysql.global_priv` SSL flags), call `Handle.UpdateAll()` then assert `RequestVerification()` and `ConnectionVerification()` pick the most-specific host row. Also cover the `UpdateAllActive()` fallback by simulating `activeUsers` > 1024 and confirming privilege results remain deterministic.
findings.what: `Handle.UpdateAll()` stores a fully-loaded privilege cache without initializing `globalVars` and without enforcing deterministic per-user ordering for tables that use first-match resolution (`global_priv`, `tables_priv`, `columns_priv`), so privilege/auth matching can select the wrong host-pattern row after `UpdateAll()`.
